requirements.text: Every evaluation context must contain nonempty scope, construct, kernel-version, parameter-set, governance-assignment, semantic-adjudication-assignment, and evidence-window identifiers.
An evaluation may not execute under a kernel version other than 3.1.0.
Every evaluated edge must resolve exactly one verified receipt for each of the fifteen governance predicates.
Governance receipts must correspond to the same object, scope, construct, kernel version, execution history, and edge.
Missing, duplicated, false, unverified, mismatched, or hash-invalid governance receipts must set HFgov true.
Every evaluated edge must resolve one verified semantic adjudication receipt containing object_real and exactly one route_class.
The engine must not infer a favorable semantic route class from a numeric score.
Every completed edge evaluation must produce exactly one disposition.
Disposition precedence must be reject, reslot, correct, hold, forward, then reject by default.
F must equal Av3 only when disposition is PASS_FORWARD and must equal zero otherwise.
Canonical record hashes must use deterministic UTF-8 JSON and SHA-256.
Nonpass dispositions must remain in history and require disposition-specific resolution records.
A rejected execution history must never become FINAL_CLOSED.
A closure suffix must contain only PASS_FORWARD edges with F at least two-thirds under one constant context.
Terminal engine, integration, value, coherence, entropy, South, and West conditions must pass before GLOCK qualification.
Lifecycle transitions must occur in the order EXECUTING, GLOCK_QUALIFIED, PROVISIONALLY_SEALED, HOME_RETURN_VERIFIED, FINAL_CLOSED.
Lifecycle stages may not be skipped, reversed, or advanced by an invalid receipt.
The only authorized claim at each lifecycle stage is the claim listed in the stage claim registry.
Executable conformance must not be represented as empirical validation, domain validation, autonomous semantic inference, universal reachability, or external mathematical review.
